Resolves #22105
Related: #21198, #21603, #22108

A detached Web Desktop app now returns to its original workspace after its native window pauses over it. The workspace outlines the eligible area and shows the remaining dwell time along its bottom edge. Moving away cancels the return. Reduced motion keeps a static outline.

Evidence: L3 (two native browser windows, physical frame geometry, destination DOM and stable component identity) → L3 required.

## AC Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Browser observation |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | Moving a committed Mail popup by its native frame and dwelling restored its original dialog ID, selected Robin Chen message and task ID, leaving exactly one window. The explicit Back button and held-pointer out-and-back also passed. |
| AC-2 | Startup already overlapping the workspace stays detached. Moving into the taskbar clears the countdown. Moving or shrinking the opener out from under the popup cancels the pending return. A foreign desktop cannot receive it. Reloading rebinds the current window ID and preserves the selected message. |
| AC-3 | The maintained Chrome regression uses browser-level frame movement and exercises cancellation and successful dwell. The physical mouse check is recorded below. |

## Deltas from ticket

Dock and Desktop share the same WindowPosition observation setup and DragCoordinator dwell. The desktop adapter exposes the original workspace bounds and checks the committed popup route again at drop. Returning invokes the existing desktop restore and focus transaction. Dock's Workspace delegates its existing observation method to NativeVesselTransaction.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Producer and consumer |
| --- | --- |
| `NativeVesselTransaction.observeWindowGeometry(windowId)` | Enables the existing movement and resize streams in the identified Main window. Dock Workspace and the Web Desktop return target both use it. |
| `Neo.desktop.NativeReturnTarget` | WindowTearOut creates one adapter for each admitted popup renderer. It registers the owner with DragCoordinator and releases the registration on renderer detach or successful body restoration. |

## Test Evidence

- The native-frame regression failed on `47118ccf83` and passed on the candidate. Chrome's DevTools Protocol moved real browser windows. Production window observers and DragCoordinator handled every subsequent move and return.
- Seven Web Desktop browser journeys passed. The desktop and WindowPosition unit suites passed 100 tests, and both Dock geometry-stream controls passed.
- Additional Chrome checks covered owning-window move and resize, a foreign desktop, reload, a held-pointer tear-out followed by native-frame return, and the cue in light and dark with both motion preferences.
- In the production build with the appearance and launcher fixes, the return countdown was active when the user signed out or revoked Mail. Both actions closed the popup and removed its task. The next account opened Help with fresh dialog and task IDs. Chrome recorded zero uncaught page or worker exceptions.
- The engine CI selector includes the maintained regression on shard 1. The workspace size baseline decreased from 1,090 to 1,089 executable lines.
- Hosted Chromium passed the native frame regression in 8.8 seconds on `398de2cee3`. The desktop theme suite identified two unset idle animation properties. After setting their neutral defaults, all 16 focused browser checks passed, including every shipped theme at desktop and phone widths and the native dwell itself.
- On the following production check, leaving the workspace cleared the visible outline but left the prior 1200 ms inline value. The maintained test reproduced it. With explicit style removal, the same test verifies both timing properties return to zero after cancellation and completion. All 16 focused browser checks passed again.

## Commits

- `c696309706` implements native return, the workspace cue and its browser regression.
- `398de2cee3` records the generated class hierarchy entry for the new desktop adapter.
- `26f49078ce` initializes both idle countdown properties to zero. The active cue still takes its duration and offset from the coordinator.
- `787976c7e5` clears the inline timing values on exit and asserts the resulting idle state.

## Manual validation

Tobi confirmed on 23 November that a released native popup reintegrated in his physical mouse walkthrough. He also confirmed that the first held-pointer exit and return worked. The second exit during that same uninterrupted drag failed and is tracked in [#22112](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/22112).

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] Repeat early cancellation by moving the native popup out of the outlined workspace in the merged build. The preview has automated coverage; manual confirmation above covers completed return.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**:
  1. **Held-titlebar close deferral (`src/desktop/WindowTearOut.mjs` `#retire` vs `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs` `settleNativeWindowDisposition`):** Because `NativeReturnTarget#suspendWindowDrag` returns `false` (`embodyNativeHover` is unset), `DragCoordinator#commitNativeWindowDrop` invokes `onRemoteDrop` -> `returnToDesktop({focus: true})` immediately when the `1200ms` dwell + `250ms` settle timer fires, even if the user is still holding the OS titlebar. Inside `WindowTearOut#retire`, `#restorePane(entry)` moves the live body home and destroys `entry.nativeReturn` before `NativeVesselTransaction.closeVessel` runs once (`6 × 50ms` poll). On any platform/window-server state that defers `win.close()` past `300ms` while the titlebar remains held (the case `DragCoordinator`'s `nativeWindowRetireRetryMs` 80-attempt loop handles via `onRemoteDropOut`), `closeVessel` resolves `false` after `#restorePane` already detached the popup's body and released `nativeReturn`, leaving an empty popup shell open after mouse release. Non-blocking for v14 given `@tobiu`'s confirmed physical mouse return on macOS, worth watching alongside #22112 if Windows/Linux window managers defer `win.close()` during active titlebar grabs.
  2. **Early-return guard in `WindowTearOut#restorePane` (`src/desktop/WindowTearOut.mjs:327-329`):** `#releaseNativeReturn(entry)` sits after `if (windowId && !this.#embodiment.restore({itemId, windowId})) return false;`. Calling `this.#releaseNativeReturn(entry)` unconditionally inside `WindowTearOut#destroy()` (or before returning on teardown) ensures `entry.nativeReturn` cannot outlive `WindowTearOut` if `embodiment.restore` ever rejects during destruction. Also minor `core-idiom-audit` note: `NativeReturnTarget#onRemoteDragMove` and `#onRemoteDragLeave` write `workspace.style` and `workspace.addCls`/`removeCls` as two sequential statements rather than a single `workspace.set({...})`.
